items.title: W4: match statement checking and lowering + expression/refutable patterns (slice 1 — integer scrutinee, constant integer expression cases, `default` — implemented; rest gated by semantics-TODO diagnostics)
items.bullet: Control flow: matching — good switch equivalents
items.notes: W4 slice 1 (fork/trial-w4/plan.md) implements the match *statement* with an integer scrutinee (Core.IntLiteral, builtin integer types, and the Int(N)/UInt(N) adapters only — other integer-repr adapter classes are gated out), constant integer expression case patterns, and a `default` arm, as an if/else-chain SemIR shape (Branch/BranchIf + convergence; no lowering changes; comparisons use the design-mandated `literal == scrutinee` operand order, docs/design/pattern_matching.md 'Expression patterns'). Bare `name: type` case bindings (including `unused`) landed in S2b (fork/match-replatform/plan.md §3.2): they check as a `ValueBindingPattern` under `Kind::MatchCaseArm`, contribute a constant-true test condition, and bind via `LocalPatternMatch` in the arm's body block. Choice alternative patterns with payload destructuring (`case .Ok(value: i32)`) landed in S2c (§3.3, tracked under W-010/W-011): a dedicated AlternativePattern parse form at the case root, discriminant test, and per-element payload bindings in the bind pass. Case guards (`case P if (E)`) landed in S2d (§3.4): the guard is checked in the arm's scope with the pattern's bindings in scope, captured in its own expression region, spliced into the arm's body block after the bind pass, and a failed guard branches to the next arm's test with the arm scope's cleanups discharged on the failure edge; the `match case guard` TODO string is discharged (all three stub sites deleted), and control_flow/match_guard_binding.carbon + project/most_features_missing_match.carbon un-SKIPped (PASS floor 74 → 77), with the new differential pair control_flow/match_guard_diff.carbon. `default`-clause guards remain a parse+check gap (W-067). Choice exhaustiveness landed in S2e (§3.5, SF-7): a choice `match` whose unguarded arms cover every alternative (per-alternative arms via the SemIR::ChoiceAlternative metadata, or an irrefutable binding arm covering everything; guarded arms never count) needs no `default`, and a non-exhaustive choice match without `default` is the real MatchNonexhaustive error naming the uncovered alternatives (fail_choice_nonexhaustive.carbon; positive goldens exhaustive_choice.carbon + exhaustive_choice_binding.carbon; conformance choice_payload_roundtrip_diff.carbon dropped its never-taken `default`). Remaining scope, each gated by a clean semantics-TODO (evidence lines): tuple/paren patterns and compile-time case bindings (the combined-string gates: handle_match.cpp's non-binding-root fallback at :547 and handle_binding_pattern.cpp's compile-time/form case gates; pinned by fail_todo_tuple_pattern.carbon), `var`/`ref` case bindings (their own TODO string at the `Kind::MatchCaseArm` gate in handle_binding_pattern.cpp, pinned to the binding), non-binding subpatterns in choice alternative payloads (the S2c `non-binding subpattern in match `case` alternative pattern` TODO at handle_match.cpp:364), non-integer and adapter-class scrutinees (MatchCondition gate, including choices with fewer than two alternatives — W-068), integer-scrutinee `match` without `default` (the `match statement without `default` arm` TODO, narrowed at S2e to the integer path only — including the genuinely-exhaustive irrefutable-binding-arm shape, a recorded conservative gate pinned by fail_todo_no_default.carbon's fail_irrefutable_binding_arm subfile), refutable-pattern rejection (expression.carbon comments at :17,:29,:41), and usefulness diagnostics (split out as W-066). Land gate: the new AUTOUPDATE goldens have no CHECK lines yet and must be autoupdated on the runner, then the scoreboard regenerated (rulebook R11/R12). Completion flips TWO scoreboard entries: control_flow/match_switch.carbon (owning bullet) and project/most_features_missing_match.carbon (bullet: Project: toolchain implements most 0.1 language features incl. C++ interop without undermining evaluation). Prerequisite for W-010/W-011/W-012/W-017. Coherence risk 2 (fork/design-sprint/README.md:182-188): pin scope to ONE shared refutable-match SemIR core that `?` (W-018) and let-else (W-012) also desugar onto.

items.title: W5a: choice alternatives with parameters (payload-carrying sum types) (slice 1 — concrete trivially-copyable payload construction, F-007k hybrid storage, discriminant-observable match via payload-free alternative patterns — implemented; specifics-as-scrutinees lifted at W5-S3a; generic payload synthesis landed at W5-S3b with per-specific layout recompute; payload destructuring on specifics — symbolic, converted, imported, guarded — landed at W5-S3c; Self-dependent and non-trivial payloads gated by diagnostics)
items.bullet: Type system: Sum types (discriminated unions)
items.notes: W5 slice 1 (fork/w5-choice/plan.md §2) implements payload-alternative construction (C.Ok(42); zero-payload Alt() function-like per SF-3), the F-007k hybrid storage contract (StructType{.discriminant, .payload: CustomLayoutType}, payload tuples overlapping at offset 0, max-of-fields size/align; payload-free choices keep the prior repr), and match over choice scrutinees with leading-dot payload-free alternative patterns + default (SF-4), all via pre-existing SemIR inst kinds plus the Class::is_choice entity flag. Remaining scope, each gated by a clean semantics-TODO or dedicated diagnostic (evidence lines): generic/Self-dependent payloads (S3), non-trivially-copyable/destructible payloads (SF-6, post-0.1 record), qualified alternative patterns (SF-4 work item), non-choice non-integer scrutinees. Payload destructuring patterns .Ok(...) landed at the match re-platform's S2c (fork/match-replatform/plan.md §3.3): dedicated AlternativePattern parse form, discriminant test + payload-tuple extraction with per-element bindings, parens-iff-parameter-list enforcement (bare .Ok on a payload alternative and .Err() on a constant alternative are now real diagnostics, not TODOs), and non-binding payload subpatterns gated by a new TODO. Land gate: the new AUTOUPDATE goldens (choice/payload_construct, choice/payload_layout, match/choice_scrutinee, match/choice_scrutinee_imported, and lower/choice/payload_layout — the F-007k anti-Goodhart layout pin, plan risk R-6) ship with no CHECK lines and must be autoupdated on the runner, then the scoreboard regenerated. S1 un-SKIPs types/choice_payload_construct.carbon and adds the choice_discriminant_diff pair. Destructuring landed at S2c (see above); exhaustiveness (SF-7) landed at S2e under W-008 — exhaustive choice matches need no `default` (MatchNonexhaustive names uncovered alternatives otherwise); choices with fewer than two alternatives stay behind the scrutinee gate (W-068). W-009 coordination per plan risk R-3: S1 built the narrow custom-layout pieces (convert.cpp ChoicePayload fill; custom_witness.cpp CustomLayoutType destroy cases); W-009 rebases on them. Review follow-ups landed on claude/carbon-fork-0-1-followups: duplicate alternative names diagnose NameDeclDuplicate/NameDeclPrevious before scope registration instead of CHECK-crashing (handle_choice.cpp; fail_duplicate_alternative.carbon), the choice-case defense-in-depth fallback now emits `match case pattern on unsupported choice alternative shape` (the scrutinee string stays on the scrutinee gate), plus the F-A1 OneShot single-payload testdata (check+lower) and the export-import multi-hop scrutinee golden — all goldens empty pending runner autoupdate (R15/R19). DONE at S2c (review follow-up (2)): the SemIR::ChoiceAlternative name-to-index side table on Class (populated in handle_choice.cpp, imported in import_ref.cpp) replaced GetAlternativeDiscriminant's constant excavation, which was deleted from pattern_match.cpp along with its GetCanonicalFileAndInstId cross-file walk. Specifics of generic choices as match scrutinees landed at W5-S3a (fork/w5-s3/plan.md, slice S3a): the GetChoiceDiscriminantType specific_id clause is deleted and the MatchCondition scrutinee gate forces the specific's definition resolution via RequireCompleteType before any repr read, so payload-free specifics (concrete, symbolic inside a generic body, and imported) dispatch by discriminant and are covered by SF-7 exhaustiveness (match/choice_generic_scrutinee.carbon, lower/testdata/match/choice_generic_scrutinee.carbon, conformance types/choice_generic_roundtrip.carbon, PASS floor 77 -> 78). Payload synthesis landed at W5-S3b (fork/w5-s3/plan.md, slice S3b): symbolic payload types synthesize — the payload region's CustomLayoutType carries the zero-alignment dependent-layout sentinel at the definition and is recomputed per specific by the now-reachable EvalConstantInst hook (eval_inst.cpp:211) — SF-6 enforcement moves to monomorphization for symbolic payloads (ChoicePayloadNotTrivialInSpecific at the forcing use, with a structural pre-filter so mutual by-value generic recursion diagnoses instead of crashing on the forward-reference CHECK), alternative constructors of a generic choice are themselves generic (MakeGeneratedFunctionDecl's build_generic bracketing), and the alternative table carries parameterized rows, CLOSING the S3a partial-table window (the pin is now choice_generic_scrutinee.carbon's fail_mixed_table_closed subfile, a MatchNonexhaustive diagnosis naming the uncovered payload alternative). The definition TODO narrowed to `choice alternative payload with Self-dependent type` (handle_choice.cpp:624; params.carbon:58, fail_generic_payload.carbon). Payload DESTRUCTURING on a concrete specific (`case .Some(v: i32)` on Opt(i32)) is reachable at S3b and pinned by the destructure subfiles of choice/generic_payload.carbon (check + lower); the generic residue CLOSED at W5-S3c (fork/w5-s3/plan.md §3 S3c, a pure verification-and-pinning slice — no toolchain code change): multi-parameter payload destructuring per specific, guarded destructuring arms, R-7 substituted binding conversions (i32 payload to i64 binding, the S2c DeferCleanups shape), imported-generic destructuring, and the R-8 symbolic-body destructure (`case .Both(a: T, b: T)` on a `P(T)` scrutinee — the scrutinee gate's forcing resolves the symbolic specific's definition through the completer's ClassType case, and GetChoicePayloadInfo's reads are purely structural on the substituted symbolic constants), all pinned by match/choice_generic_payload_pattern.carbon (check + lower; the lower golden pins per-specific ELEMENT offsets — byte 4 vs byte 8 for the second payload element — and the instantiated symbolic-body destructure), every positive match exhaustive without `default` plus a fail_nonexhaustive_payload coverage pin. The sum_types.md example runs as conformance control_flow/choice_generic_roundtrip_diff (std::optional C++ oracle): declaration and match verbatim; the doc's `var ... = Optional(i32).None` line cannot compile (initializing a `var` from a class value copies, and choices implement no `Core.Copy` — the S1-recorded gap), so None binds with `let` while the doc's re-assignment line runs verbatim — recorded as a dated amendment to plan §3 S3c. Conformance: the types/choice_generic_diff pair landed at S3b (PASS floor 79 -> 80 over 111), including a runtime-computed discriminant/payload collision probe; choice_generic_roundtrip_diff lands at S3c (PASS floor 80 -> 81 over 112) and carries the collision payload into payload READBACK.

items.notes: Scope trade recorded at fork/match-replatform/plan.md §3.4 and re-recorded at the S2d landing: design authority allows `default if (E) => ...` (so `default` stays equivalent to `case _: auto`), but the fork's parser attaches guard nodes only to `case` — `HandleMatchDefaultIntroducer` goes straight to the handler block with no guard production. The check side is small once parse carries the nodes: a guarded `default` arm reuses the S2d capture-splice-branch shape with no pattern test and no bindings, and its else edge needs a following arm or another `default` to fall through to, so the exhaustiveness interaction (a guarded `default` never discharges the `default` requirement) should land with or after S2e. S2e landed (2026-08-08) with coverage recording in MatchCase and the analysis in MatchStatement, so the check-side hook points exist; when this lands, a guarded `default` must record nothing into Context::MatchStatementContext, exactly like a guarded `case`.

items.title: S2e follow-up: `match` over choices with fewer than two alternatives (single-alternative and empty choices)
items.bullet: Control flow: matching — sum-type consumption incl. std::variant/std::optional interop
evidence: fork/decision-log.md (W5-S1 fewer-than-two-alternatives bullet + S2e and W5-S3a landing notes, 2026-08-08)
items.notes: Recorded at W5-S1 ('S2's exhaustiveness work is the natural place to admit them') and explicitly NOT discharged at S2e: plan §3.5 sanctions only the MatchStatement exhaustiveness analysis, and these choices have an empty-tuple discriminant — GetChoiceDiscriminantType requires an integer discriminant, so they fail the MatchCondition scrutinee gate (`match on unsupported scrutinee type`). Admitting them is scrutinee-gate + dispatch work, not coverage arithmetic: a single-alternative choice needs an always-taken arm with no discriminant test (constant-true condition, payload extraction still real for a payload alternative), and an empty choice needs a vacuously-exhaustive zero-arm match (parse currently requires at least one case or `default`). The S2e coverage machinery (Context::MatchStatementContext) already handles the exhaustiveness half once the gate admits them. W5-S3a's specifics-as-scrutinees lift composes with this gate rather than widening it: single-alternative and empty SPECIFICS of generic choices (Always(i32), Never(i32)) still fail the integer-discriminant check and keep the scrutinee TODO, pinned by choice_generic_scrutinee.carbon's fail_todo_single_alternative_specific and fail_todo_empty_choice_specific subfiles; discharging this item must flip those pins too.

items.title: W5-S3b follow-up: cross-file references to file-scope `let` bindings have no lowering story (upstream gap, surfaced by choice work)
items.bullet: Values and expressions: global bindings — file-scope `let` across libraries
evidence: toolchain/lower/testdata/var/import.carbon:46 (upstream TODO: 'lowering a reference to an imported `let` asserts')
toolchain/lower/function_context.cpp:171-196 (GetValue: imported-let refs fall through locals_ and global_variables() to the constant path and CHECK on a non-concrete value)
toolchain/check/testdata/match/choice_generic_payload_scrutinee.carbon (imported_global split, re-authored from `let g` to `var g` because of this gap)
toolchain/lower/testdata/var/import.carbon (the supported cross-file vehicle: `var` through exported VarStorage globals)
items.notes: Surfaced by W5-S3b: once the generic-choice constructor rework made plib's `let g: P(i64) = P(i64).Neither;` check successfully, the importing file's `match (g)` crashed in lowering (function_context.cpp:190 — ImportRefLoaded with non-concrete value 'runtime'). This is not a choice bug: upstream has no cross-file runtime-global story for `let` at all — a `let` has no VarStorage, a class-typed `let` binds its value through a runtime temporary even when the initializer is constant, and the importer has no path that routes an ImportRefLoaded of a `let` binding to the defining file's backing storage the way `var` routes through the exported VarStorage global. The R-2 counter-program split was re-authored to `var g` (imported_global) rather than silently dropping the cross-file scrutinee coverage; restoring a `let`-based split is the acceptance test for discharging this item. Half (b) of the fix landed with the W5-S3b import-crash round (import_ref.cpp, TryResolveInstCanonical's non-constant-binding branch): an imported binding whose BOUND VALUE is constant now resolves to that value's constant — translated with its generic attachment intact — so constant-bound `let`s and choice-alternative wrapper bindings import as constants and lower through the constant path. The residual gap is (a): a `let` bound to a RUNTIME value still has no exported backing storage (the materialized temporary would need promotion to a named global, referenced cross-file like VarStorage). Restoring a runtime-`let`-based cross-file split is the acceptance test for the residue.

items.notes: Recorded at the B1b third fix round (fork/decision-log.md B1 landing note, 2026-08-08). The desugar's carrier temporary gets the STANDARD statement-end/return-path cleanup discharge; for a symbolic operand the carrier is a symbolic `Core.ControlFlow` specific, and the discharge's `Core.Destroy` lookup fails eagerly because `CanDestroyType` needs every payload element destroyable while `Try` places no `Destroy` bound on `ContinueType`/`BreakType`. Candidate resolutions, decided outside a fix round (interface-contract change → veto digest / S3p round): (a) bound the `Try` associated constants (`let ContinueType: Destroy;`-style, the `Iterate` precedent — every user impl's `forall` params then need `Destroy` bounds); (b) teach the destroy machinery that an SF-6-admissible choice specific is trivially destructible even under symbolic args (the payload allowlist is a per-specific guarantee the symbolic path could trust structurally); or (c) a deferred-destroy mechanism for symbolic specifics. Discharge test: restore question.carbon's generic split POSITIVE (the pre-gate body `let unused c: R.ContinueType = r?; return R.FromBreak(0);`) and delete the gate + fail_todo_generic pin.
